story.title: The Last Bookmark
story.logline: A woman discovers her library books are returning themselves with margin notes written in her own future handwriting.
story.twist: The notes are not warnings from her future self, but suicide countdowns she is subconsciously writing.
story.ending: If every page is already written, who is holding the pen?

scenes.narration: My library book returned itself yesterday. Inside the back cover, a margin note written in my exact handwriting said: page twelve.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 25-year-old woman with messy dark hair and a gray oversized hoodie holding an open hardcover book in a dimly lit apartment.
scenes.camera: Vertical medium shot focusing on the book margins.

scenes.narration: I opened page twelve with shaking fingers. A single sentence stared back at me, predicting every word I would speak today.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie staring wide-eyed at the book pages in the dim apartment.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on her terrified eyes, then dropping to the page.

scenes.narration: I tried to defy the book. I stayed silent all afternoon. But the margin note had already predicted my silence.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie sitting rigidly on a worn couch, refusing to speak.
scenes.camera: Vertical wide shot tracking her tense posture.

scenes.narration: Panic pulled me back to the library. The old librarian smiled, sliding three more stacks across the wooden desk.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie standing at a towering wooden library desk facing an elderly clerk.
scenes.camera: Over-the-shoulder shot framing the tall stacks of books.

scenes.narration: Every single book bore my handwriting. Each volume chronicled the final hours of my life, chapter by terrifying chapter.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie frantically flipping through dozens of books on a library table.
scenes.camera: Vertical fast-paced tracking shot around the table.

scenes.narration: Chapter seven described this exact room, the flickering fluorescent light, and the cold metal of the emergency exit.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie under a buzzing fluorescent light in a narrow hallway.
scenes.camera: Low angle looking up at her face bathed in harsh light.

scenes.narration: I grabbed a pen, determined to rewrite the ending. If I crossed out the final chapter, I could break the cycle.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie gripping a black pen, aggressively scribbling across book pages.
scenes.camera: Close-up on the frantic hand movements and shredded paper.

scenes.narration: The ink bled through the paper, revealing text underneath that I hadn't written yet, but my hand was moving.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie watching her own hand write words against her conscious will.
scenes.camera: High angle looking directly down at the moving hand.

scenes.narration: My eyes widened as I realized the cruel truth. I wasn't reading my future. I was authoring my own demise.
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie freezing mid-stroke, realization dawning on her pale face.
scenes.camera: Vertical extreme close-up on her tearful eyes.

scenes.narration: The final page was blank, waiting for my final stroke. If every page is already written, who is holding the pen?
scenes.visual_prompt: The same 25-year-old woman with dark hair and a gray hoodie holding the pen over a completely blank final page in darkness.
scenes.camera: Static wide shot holding on the solitary figure in shadow.

caption.hook: My future handwriting. My final countdown.
caption.title: The Last Bookmark
caption.caption: For weeks, my library returns came back with mysterious notes in my own handwriting. I thought my future self was sending warnings. Until I realized I was counting down my final days.
